key_insight: HVAF-sprayed Tribaloy-400 formed a denser, more protective oxide scale than detonation-sprayed coating, giving better resistance to molten solar-salt hot corrosion at 500 °C.
engineering_relevance: For CSP thermal storage containers, HVAF appears to be the more reliable deposition route for extending coating life and reducing salt-driven degradation.
method: Tribaloy-400 coatings were deposited on ASTM A516 steel using HVAF and detonation spraying.
Samples were exposed to 60% NaNO3–40% KNO3 molten solar salt at 500 °C for up to 1000 h.
Corrosion/oxidation behavior was assessed using phase analysis, SEM, elemental mapping, and mass-gain/spallation observations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that HVAF retained a uniform Cr–Mo–Si–O enriched surface with minimal salt penetration after 1000 h, while DS showed deeper ingress, higher mass gain, and more spallation.
watch_item: The study is specific to one substrate, one salt composition, and one temperature, so performance may differ under real CSP cycling and mixed-impurity conditions.
paper_title: Hot corrosion behavior of thermal sprayed using HVAF and DS techniques with Tribaloy-400 coatings for solar energy storage container
